question: How many different drivers will win a Grand Prix in the 2026 F1 season?

calls.reasoning: As of 2026-10-14, 17 of 23 Grands Prix have been run. Six different drivers have won: Antonelli 8, Russell 3, Norris 2, Verstappen 2, Hamilton 1, Leclerc 1 (formula1.com results page). So '5' can't happen. Six races are left: USA, Mexico, Brazil, Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The likely new winners are Piastri and Hadjar. Piastri has 2 podiums and none since Miami; Hadjar has 3 third places. Polymarket's US Grand Prix markets put Hadjar at about 3% and Verstappen at 42%, but volumes are only a few hundred dollars. The four cars from Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren already have winners, so a new winner needs a teammate to get through or a chaotic race. That chance is about 6-9% per race, which gives roughly 35-40% for at least one new winner over six races. Two or more new winners comes out at about 5%.

- Resolves off the ESPN 2026 results page (number of distinct GP winners). Sprint races don't count.
- Event window: whole 2026 season, through the Abu Dhabi GP on Dec 6. As of 2026-10-14, 17 of 23 races are done (about 74%).

calls.reconciliation: Factual points were mostly agreed: 6 distinct winners and 6 races left. Disputed factual items: Verstappen's win count (2 vs 3) does not affect the distinct-winner count; I did not resolve it. My one search confirmed that Verstappen won Singapore, that Hadjar drives for Red Bull (10th from the pit lane), and that Piastri was 5th, consistent with the runs. The remaining dispute is pure judgment: the per-race hazard, with the runs at 5-9%. Because the pool of new winners is only two weak contenders, I took ~5.5% per race, landing between Run 2 and Run 3.
